item: Bootstrap (shell's first call: identity, workspaces with unread counts, models, providers, limits, feature flags)
Workspace shell (placements, nav for one workspace)
Chat turn start (JSON or multipart with attachments), SSE stream of the turn
Conversation event stream (resume or replay an in-flight turn from `afterSeq`)
Identity event stream (workspace/notification/connector events for the signed-in user)
Workspace tool call (the shell's one write door)
Identity tool call (tools that need no workspace: profile, workspace management, personal connectors)
Workspace file download (Range passed through, host headers)
Upload files to a workspace (multipart, optional conversationId tag)
App UI resource proxy (an app's inlined HTML, gzip + weak ETag, revalidate each use)
MCP door, per workspace (2026-07-28 revision only)
Run key set (JWKS a gateway checks turn credentials against)
Brand script for the login page
JSON 404 fallback and central error handler
Host allowlist for the routes answered without sign-in
Rate limits: chat, tool call, MCP (`NB_CHAT_RATE_LIMIT`, `NB_TOOL_RATE_LIMIT`, `NB_MCP_RATE_LIMIT`)
Body limits (1 MB JSON, the chat and upload limits, the server ceiling)
Request metrics and tracing (route-pattern labels, OTel spans)
Provider selection from `instance.json` (`auth.adapter`: dev, oidc, workos); no instance file means no provider
OIDC provider: auth-code + PKCE, refresh, JWKS verification, OIDC bearer treated as first-party
WorkOS provider (AuthKit): sessions, user directory, authorization server for MCP clients (`WORKOS_API_KEY`)
Token grants: a first-party session vs a resource token whose audience must name `/mcp/<wsId>`
Run keys: turn credentials signed per run (model gateway, ACP worker audiences)
Tenant service-token mint from the fleet authorizer (`NB_FLEET_AUTHORIZER_TOKEN_URL`)
Auth-failure audit event (`audit.auth_failure`); a transient verification failure is not audited
`plugins` (engine only: system plugins, `false` turns off conversations, tasks or files, `servers.<key>.url`, `transferOrigins`)
`NB_TIMEZONE` (the instance default timezone for schedules without one; the tasks server falls back to `Pacific/Honolulu`)
Shell tour, release banner, telemetry consent, keyboard shortcuts, help menu, user menu, mobile drawer
`tasks__update` as a patch (`null` clears, omitted keeps)
One-off run from an inline definition
Once schedule (`at`) and a missed once
Event schedule (`match` with debounce and fire ceiling)
Admin routing of notifications to a task (the only event path), including inbound webhooks (src/hooks) through notifications
`enabled:false` pauses the schedule and events; `run` still runs it
No schedule: runs only on demand
A run fires as its owner, walled to the task's workspace
Membership re-checked each run; a removed or deactivated owner
`allowedTools` globs bound what the run can reach
Authoring tools refused inside an unattended run
`allowedTools` naming a tasks authoring tool refused at write time
Declared `skills` loaded before the first model call
Per-run caps (`maxIterations`, `maxInputTokens`, `maxRunDurationMs`) lowered to the operator's ceilings
Token budget (daily, monthly or lifetime) through spend accounts; a spent budget disables
Run admission: global slots (`maxConcurrentRuns`), a bounded queue (`maxQueuedRuns`), fair share between workspaces
Failure backoff and auto-disable after a streak (transient failures counted separately)
Activity log per run (tool name, ok, why, ms; never input or output)
Execution and label vocabulary, derived on read
Estimated cost per day on a task summary
Batch budget as one USD spend account; `exceeds_share`
Batch runs leave the task's schedule alone and bypass the one-run-per-task rule
Run-failed notice, once per failing stretch
Notice wording and naming in the inbox
On-disk tasks at `workspaces/<ws>/tasks/<owner>/` read at boot
Scheduled screen `ui://tasks/panel` (sidebar "Scheduled", route `@nimblebraininc/tasks`): home, task page, editor, schedule picker, runs, result, activity, batch pane
Task-authoring guide: a chat skill bound to `tasks__*` and the MCP server `instructions`
Grant / revoke personal connector into workspace
Boot start of every workspace's connectors
Gateway transport credential (hosted MCP vendor key)
